# Fundamental Group of the Disk with Boundary Rotation Identification

## Setup

Let $X = D^2/\sim$ where on $\partial D^2 = S^1$ we identify $z \sim e^{i\pi/n}z$. The rotation $z \mapsto e^{i\pi/n}z$ generates a cyclic group $G \cong \mathbb{Z}_{2n}$ acting on $S^1$ (since $2n \cdot (\pi/n) = 2\pi$, the order is $2n$). The image of the boundary in $X$ is the quotient $C = S^1/G \cong S^1$.

## Applying Seifert–van Kampen

Choose $\varepsilon > 0$ small and define two open subsets of $X$:

- **$U$** = image of $\{|z| < 1 - \varepsilon/2\}$ — an open disk, hence **contractible**, so $\pi_1(U) = 0$.
- **$V$** = image of $\{1 - \varepsilon < |z| \leq 1\}$ — an annular collar of the boundary with the identification on the outer edge. This deformation retracts (radially) onto the boundary quotient $C \cong S^1$, so $\pi_1(V) \cong \mathbb{Z}$, generated by a single loop $b$ around $C$.
- **$U \cap V$** = image of $\{1-\varepsilon < |z| < 1-\varepsilon/2\}$ — an open annulus (no identification here), deformation retracting to $S^1$, so $\pi_1(U \cap V) \cong \mathbb{Z}$, generated by a loop $a$ going once around the inner circle.

## The Inclusion Maps

**Inclusion $i_1: U\cap V \hookrightarrow U$.** Since $U$ is contractible, $i_1(a) = 0$.

**Inclusion $i_2: U\cap V \hookrightarrow V$.** Under the radial deformation retraction of $V$ onto the outer boundary $S^1$, the generator loop $a$ (one traversal of the inner circle $e^{i\theta}$, $\theta: 0\to 2\pi$, at radius $1-\varepsilon$) is pushed to the loop $e^{i\theta}$, $\theta: 0 \to 2\pi$, on the outer boundary. The quotient map $q: S^1 \to C \cong S^1$ sends $e^{i\theta} \mapsto e^{i\,2n\theta}$ (since each orbit $\{e^{i(\theta + k\pi/n)}\}_{k=0}^{2n-1}$ is identified with $e^{i\,2n\theta}$). Therefore the image loop traverses $C$ exactly **$2n$ times**:

$$i_2(a) = b^{2n}.$$

## Computing the Amalgamation

Seifert–van Kampen gives

$$\pi_1(X) \cong \bigl(\pi_1(U) * \pi_1(V)\bigr) \big/ N$$

where $N$ is the normal subgroup generated by $i_1(g)\,i_2(g)^{-1}$ for all $g \in \pi_1(U\cap V)$. With $\pi_1(U)=0$ and $\pi_1(V)=\langle b\rangle \cong \mathbb{Z}$:

$$N = \langle\!\langle\, i_1(a)\,i_2(a)^{-1}\,\rangle\!\rangle = \langle\!\langle\, 0 \cdot b^{-2n}\,\rangle\!\rangle = \langle\!\langle\, b^{2n}\,\rangle\!\rangle.$$

Therefore

$$\pi_1(X) \cong \mathbb{Z} \big/ \langle b^{2n}\rangle \cong \mathbb{Z}_{2n}.$$

## Sanity Check

For $n=1$: the identification is $z \sim -z$ (antipodal on $S^1$), giving $\mathbb{RP}^2$, whose fundamental group is $\mathbb{Z}_2 = \mathbb{Z}_{2\cdot 1}$. ✓

## Result

$$\boxed{\pi_1(X) \cong \mathbb{Z}_{2n}}$$

The fundamental group of the unit disk with each boundary point identified with the point $\pi/n$ radians away is the **cyclic group of order $2n$**.

### PROOF COMPLETE
